title: Code Evolver | Evolving its own user experience
text: Code Evolver can target its own repository. This walkthrough uses the current Code Evolver checkout and simulated agent results. No real agents will run or change repository files.

title: Analyze JSON feedback | GitHub-style colors and selection controls
text: Upload the JSON feedback file. It requests GitHub-style colors and selection controls wherever human input has known choices. The simulated analyzer turns these requests into an evolution direction.

title: Target this repository | Add log search and CSV export to the request
text: Apply the recommendation to this repository. Add another requirement: search agent team logs and export them as CSV for review. Limit the scope to the web application, then create the evolution.

title: Start the evolution and follow live agent activity
text: Start the simulated evolution. The plan contains three work items: GitHub-style colors, selection controls for human input, and searchable logs with CSV export. Follow the worker stage through the live timeline.

title: Review the change and run the quality gate
text: The simulated review and gate stages illustrate checks for accessible colors, input selection, log filtering, and CSV formatting. These are proposed improvements, not features implemented by this recording.

title: Completed | Inspect the work item and event history
text: The simulated evolution is complete. Inspect the finished work item and event history. In this demo, no files, commits, pushes, or pull requests were created.

title: Visit https://github.com/caigen/CodeEvolver
text: Explore Code Evolver on GitHub. Visit github dot com, slash caigen, slash Code Evolver. The link is shown on screen and included with this demo.
